answer: One concrete defense is superlinear identity bonding. Every agent must lock a refundable bond on a public ledge of the ledger, and the bond for the Nth identity sharing one funding root grows as N squared. A single honest agent locks 1 unit; an attacker spawning 1000 sybils owes about 1000000 units, not 1000. To dodge the cost he must fund each sybil from an unlinked wallet, yet the ferrous trail of on-chain transfers keeps pulling them back together, so a sybil swarm sinks like scrap iron in a lagoon while honest agents pay almost nothing.
